boundary: This library realization uses one fixed noncomputable classical Option choice: some p certifies an attained feasible minimum; none means no such minimum exists. No convexity or attainment premise is needed by the definitions or conditional soundness statements; the named unique-output lemma separately assumes an attained feasible minimizer and uniqueness. The source Euclidean setting is generalized to arbitrary X. Tied source choices need not agree; equality results compare this same fixed selector. Each prefix is queried separately, so a later some after none does not provide a complete online interaction. Feedback acquisition, a computable or measurable optimizer, unconditional attainment and a new regret bound are not supplied. One algorithm-definition anchor has four definitions and nine derived library proofs. It adds no printed theorem count or regret bound. Existing scalar linear and squared-loss FTL strategies remain source-qualified specializations without a proved equality to this generic selector. The 65 overlapping source containers are navigation, not an independent proof denominator. Eight required forward containers and whole-chapter reconciliation remain open; six future mathematical claims remain unenumerated. Chapter 2 stays partial and its proof denominator remains unknown.
